title: Trust centre
intro: What we do with data, who processes it, and what is done versus planned. Where something is planned, it says planned.

sections.heading: Security controls
sections.body: The control list lives in SECURITY.md in the repository and maps each control to the code or test that enforces it.
points: Every privileged action is written to an append-only audit log with actor, role and reason, mirrored to the av.audit.v1 Kafka topic. Status: built.
Role-based access with four roles: admin, ops, auditor, read-only. Status: built.
Single sign-on for the console (OIDC first, SAML-ready). Status: in progress.
Encryption in transit (TLS at ingress, Kafka TLS, Postgres verify-full in production values). Status: configured in the Helm chart.
Field-level encryption of transcripts and audio references at rest. Status: built. Per-tenant envelope encryption with a managed KMS: planned.
No training or fine-tuning on client data. There is no training code path; it is a contract term with every sub-processor.
PII and payment-credential redaction before speech-to-text output reaches the model or storage, and inside the logger. Status: built and tested.
No card, CVV, UPI PIN or OTP field exists in any contract or table. A static test proves it.
Dependency audit and secret scan in CI. SAST, container scanning and signed images: planned.

sections.heading: Data flow
sections.body: A booking event from Agoda is checked against the holdout and eleven compliance gates. Only a cleared call is dialled. Speech is transcribed, redacted, and only then passed to the model with purpose-limited booking fields. Payment happens on an Agoda-hosted page linked over WhatsApp; the call never takes card details. Outcomes and redacted transcripts are stored encrypted, and handoffs land in the client's CRM.

sections.heading: Sub-processors
sections.body: None is contracted yet. Each role has exactly one provider chosen at boot, and the production validator refuses to start if a provider's region is outside the client's allowlist (India by default). The full table, with what each provider sees, is in docs/subprocessors.md.
points: Speech-to-text: Sarvam (planned), or a self-hosted model on the client's cluster.
Text-to-speech: Sarvam Bulbul (planned), or self-hosted.
Language model: one of OpenAI or Anthropic under a no-training agreement (planned), or a self-hosted model.
Telephony: Plivo or Exotel through SIP (planned).
WhatsApp: Meta WhatsApp Cloud API (planned).
CRM: the client's Zendesk, Salesforce or HubSpot tenant.

sections.heading: Retention
sections.body: Retention is set per purpose and enforced by a nightly purge that logs how many records it removed.
points: Call audio: [[spec:retention.audio_days|30 days]] by default.
Redacted transcripts: [[spec:retention.transcript_days|180 days]] by default.
Security and audit logs: [[spec:retention.ict_log_days|180 days]] rolling, kept in India, as CERT-In directs.
Consent records: as the law requires; the exact period is a question for counsel.

sections.heading: Data processing agreement
sections.body: A draft DPA template is published at /legal/dpa. It is a draft pending review by Indian counsel and is not yet signed with anyone.

sections.heading: Compliance status
sections.body: This is engineering status, not legal advice. Indian counsel must sign off before any live call.
points: TRAI TCCCPR as amended (including the Third Amendment notified [[S-24|18 Sep 2026]]): every rule we know of has an automated test. Counsel sign-off: pending.
DPDP Act 2023 and Rules 2025: built to the full standard now; core duties apply from [[S-25|13 May 2027]]. Counsel sign-off: pending.
CERT-In directions: incident timers and log retention built. Counsel sign-off: pending.
ISO 27001, SOC 2 and similar certifications: none held. Not planned before a pilot.
OWASP ASVS Level 2: used as our checklist; self-assessment in progress.

sections.heading: Reporting a vulnerability
sections.body: Email the security contact listed in /.well-known/security.txt. Please do not open a public issue. We acknowledge reports and will tell you what we changed.
